options.metric: Annual number of motorist deaths reported in crashes
options.reason: A raw annual fatality count directly shows the changing burden of motorist deaths in reported crashes.
options.answer: Recorded motorist deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025 (26.4%), but this does not establish lower risk per mile because miles driven are absent.
options.interpretation: This dataset cannot answer whether motorist death risk per mile declined because it has no miles-driven exposure; this framing answers only whether recorded motorist deaths changed. The count fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, a 26.4% decline, although it fluctuated substantially and peaked at 139 in 2020. Annual deaths are a direct measure of fatality burden in the crash records, but without an exposure denominator they do not measure risk. No in-window rows are excluded for NULL crash dates or motorist-fatality values (0 of 2,132,218, or 0%); no partial year is included, and all partial-year rows from 2012 (100,545; 4.43% of the file) and 2026 (36,424; 1.60%) are outside the date filter.

options.metric: Motorist deaths per 1,000 reported crash records
options.denominator: All dated reported crash records in that calendar year
options.reason: Normalizing by reported crash records compares fatality counts with the annual volume of crashes represented in the file.
options.answer: Motorist deaths per 1,000 reported crash records rose from 0.54 in 2013 to 0.95 in 2025 (75.4%), so this crash-normalized proxy did not decline, but it is not risk per mile.
options.interpretation: This dataset cannot answer whether motorist death risk per mile declined because it has no miles-driven exposure; this framing instead compares deaths with the number of reported crash records. The rate rose from 0.54 deaths per 1,000 records in 2013 to 0.95 in 2025, a 75.4% increase. This is a defensible crash-severity comparison because it adjusts fatality counts for the volume of reported crash records, but it leaves exposure-adjusted, per-mile risk unanswered. No in-window rows are excluded for NULL crash dates or motorist-fatality values (0 of 2,132,218, or 0%); no partial year is included, and all partial-year rows from 2012 (100,545; 4.43% of the file) and 2026 (36,424; 1.60%) are outside the date filter.
